root_idea.summary: The root centers on thrusting or piercing something with an object that penetrates it.
root_idea.development: From physical piercing and thrusting, the root extends to reciprocal spear-fighting and figurative verbal attack; related Classical usages also develop around entering, traversing, and being struck by plague.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form طَعَنَ.
Displayed separately as the Quran-attested verbal noun طَعْن.

senses.definition: To assail, blame, censure, or defame with words; to speak against.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, this verbal-attack construction occurs with فِي and is directed at religion, as in طَعَنُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ. It is figurative verbal attack rather than physical piercing.

senses.definition: Verbal assailing, blaming, censuring, or defaming; a spoken attack.
senses.usage_conditions: In طَعْنًا فِي الدِّينِ, the verbal noun denotes impugning or attacking religion with words, not piercing with a weapon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pierce, stab, thrust at, smite, or wound with a spear or similar object; also to goad or poke with a stick or the like.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The physical action does not necessarily entail that the weapon fully enters the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Piercing, stabbing, or thrusting with a spear or similar weapon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of the physical sense of طَعَنَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be smitten by plague or pestilence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported of a man and also of a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a child, to raise or thrust the head toward the mother’s breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction describing movement toward the breast.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a tree branch, to incline into or against a house while rising or extending sideways.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the direction and extension of a branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a reported expression of disapproval, to enter within the curtain; alternatively, according to another explanation, to strike the curtain with the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is transmitted with these two interpretations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go into, penetrate, and traverse the desert.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of entering or penetrating into something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To journey throughout the whole night; with a people or party, to travel by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the night or with a traveling group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become old or advanced in age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use with age as the domain entered or advanced through.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To begin or enter upon a thing or affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be an affair or thing of any kind; طَعَنَتْ فِي الحَيْضَةِ refers to entering the days of menstruation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, to strain the rein by thrusting the head forward and thereby hasten or quicken its pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse’s forward movement against the rein.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To die, or to be at the point of death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related expression طُعِنَ فِي نَيْطِهِ has the same meaning; the wording is figurative.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic use of the noun الطِّعَان.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pierce or thrust one another in war; to engage in mutual spear-fighting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form VI reciprocal construction expresses participation by two sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pierce or thrust one another in war; to engage in mutual spear-fighting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII reciprocal counterpart of تَطَاعَنَ, explicitly associated with the same construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single piercing thrust or stab, and the wound or effect produced by such a thrust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a spear-thrust or similar penetrating attack.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who habitually attacks people’s reputations with blame, censure, reproach, backbiting, or similar speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive personal description, especially in the expression طَعَّانٌ فِي أَعْرَاضِ النَّاسِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Skilled at piercing or thrusting with a spear in war.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive description of prowess in spear-fighting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epidemic disease, especially plague or pestilence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is classically connected with the idea of piercing and is also explained as a form of widespread mortality caused by epidemic disease.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or point of piercing or thrusting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of place, also used as a verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A point or ground at which someone’s reputation may be attacked, blamed, censured, or spoken against.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the idiom مَا فِيهِ مَطْعَنٌ and related expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who frequently pierces or thrusts the enemy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A vigorous personal description associated with warfare.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Smitten, pierced, or wounded by a spear or similar weapon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of one subjected to the physical action of طَعَنَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Smitten by plague or pestilence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or transferred passive-participial use associated with طَاعُون.

cautions: The internal QAC verb lemma is normalized from طَعَنُ to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form طَعَنَ; the nominal is presented as the verbal noun طَعْن.
The two Quranic occurrences express verbal attack or defamation concerning religion; physical piercing is a separate Classical branch.
The reported طَعَنَتْ فِي الخِدْرِ expression has two transmitted interpretations, both retained here.
